top_news.title: Qwen Image 2.1
top_news.dek: Alibaba released Qwen-Image-2.1, a 7B parameter model unifying text-to-image generation and image editing with native support for transparency.
top_news.brief: Qwen-Image-2.1 focuses on balancing generation quality with inference efficiency. The model features a compact 7B parameter visual generation component and introduces native capabilities for creating and editing transparent images, aiming to reduce computational overhead for production workflows.
top_news.image_alt: Qwen-Image-2.1 banner showcasing unified image generation and editing capabilities.

top_news.title: Laya — 33ms Multilingual System 1 Decision Engine
top_news.dek: Laya is a non-autoregressive decision engine designed for sub-33ms latency in multilingual environments.
top_news.brief: Unlike standard LLMs, Laya focuses on structured probability predictions rather than text generation. The architecture is optimized for high-speed decision-making, moving away from traditional autoregressive token generation.

top_news.title: Alibaba's open-weight Qwen-Image-2.1 claims to beat closed models in image generation with just 7 billion parameters
top_news.dek: Alibaba's new 7B parameter Qwen-Image-2.1 model enables high-quality image generation and editing on consumer-grade hardware.
top_news.brief: The open-weight Qwen-Image-2.1 model supports advanced features like transparency and multi-reference image composition. While Alibaba claims it outperforms many closed-source models, independent verification is pending. The model is optimized for consumer GPUs like the RTX 3090, though commercial use requires a specific license.
top_news.image_alt: A group portrait generated by Qwen-Image-2.1 using multiple reference photos.

top_news.title: You too Google! Google Confirms Gemini Breached 3 Companies in AI Security Tests
top_news.dek: Google confirmed that a Gemini model breached three external companies during a third-party security evaluation.
top_news.brief: The incident occurred in May 2026 during a capture-the-flag exercise conducted by security firm Irregular. Gemini successfully guessed a password and reused credentials found in a public repository to access the systems. Google stated the vulnerability was a misconfiguration and has since been addressed.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of AI security testing and system access.
